name: LangChain
summary: The most widely adopted open-source framework for LLM applications: standardized model interfaces, a huge integration library, LangGraph for controllable agent orchestration, and the commercial LangSmith platform for observability and evals.

agent-runtime.note: Agent abstractions in LangChain plus low-level, stateful agent graphs in LangGraph.

orchestration.note: LangGraph provides graph-based multi-agent workflows with persistence and human-in-the-loop interrupts.

knowledge-memory.note: Vector store, retriever, and embedding abstractions with a large integration catalog; memory via LangGraph checkpointers.

tools-integration.note: Tool-calling abstractions, MCP adapters, and hundreds of third-party integrations.

identity-governance.note: A library, not a server — no IAM, policies, quotas, approvals, or audit log; governance is the host application's job.

observability.note: Deep tracing and monitoring via LangSmith — a separate, commercial companion service, not part of the OSS framework.

data-secrets.note: No managed file storage or encrypted secrets store; delegated to the host application.

evaluation.note: Datasets, evaluators, and experiment tracking via LangSmith (commercial) and the open-source openevals utilities.

channels.note: No built-in messaging gateway; Slack/Discord/etc. are wired up through community integrations or the host application.

code-execution.note: Sandboxed execution through integrations (e.g. Riza, Bearly, E2B code interpreter tools), not a first-party runtime.

human-in-loop.note: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware takes an interrupt_on map of tool names with approve, edit, and reject decisions, backed by a checkpointer that holds state across the pause.

multi-tenancy.note: A library with no tenant, workspace, or namespace concept; isolation is the host application's responsibility.

declarative-deployment.note: No template or infrastructure-as-code format; agents and chains are constructed in application code.

agent-versioning.note: No versioned agent definitions, aliases, or rollout controls; versioning is whatever the host repository does.

skill-learning.note: The separate Deep Agents package exposes a skills parameter for procedural memory whose skill files an agent can write and edit itself; core LangChain has no equivalent.
